title: Exploring the cyber world: the innovation of the cristal booklet to improve speaking literacy skills and critical thinking for elementary school students
abstract: This study aims to examine the contribution of the CRISTAL Booklet (Critical Reading, Interactive Speaking, and Technology-Assisted Learning) to improving the speaking literacy and critical thinking skills of fifth-grade students who participated in the study. Speaking, literacy, and critical thinking are important skills that students need to develop. However, there are still challenges in applying these skills in the classroom. The CRISTAL Booklet was designed as a multimodal learning medium that combines critical reading, interactive speaking, and technology to enrich students’ learning experiences. This study used a quantitative approach with a one-group pretest-posttest research design. The participants were fifth-grade students from an elementary school. The research instruments included a pretest and a posttest to measure students’ speaking literacy and critical thinking skills. The results showed that the CRISTAL Booklet improved students’ speaking literacy and critical thinking skills, with a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Empowering preservice teachers’ pck development through resource folio pck development tools: Cores and pap-ers
abstract: Effective teaching entails PCK, enabling teachers to integrate different elements of instructional design in dynamic ways. The tacit nature of PCK poses challenges for novice teachers in understanding the reasons behind certain pedagogical approaches throughout the teaching-learning process. Resource Folio, as one of the PCK development tools that combines Content Representations (CoRes) and Pedagogical and Professional-experience Repertoires (PaP-eRs), is expected to be the solution for capturing teachers’ implicit pedagogical reasoning embedded in instructional design. This study investigates the use of the Resource Folio in developing and refining topic-specific PCK. 27 4th- to 6th-grade teachers in Tangerang were surveyed. The analysis of CoRes and PaP-eRs across the additional files reveals that teachers consistently use CoRes as a forward-planning pedagogical tool to align content knowledge, instructional strategies, and anticipated student difficulties, and PaP-eRs highlight teachers’ real-time decisions when students struggle, ask unexpected questions, or display alternative ways of thinking. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Transforming learning quality in elementary schools through the reflective action model in values-based instructional management
abstract: This study investigates the implementation of the Reflective Action model within values-based instructional management to improve learning quality and character development in elementary education. The research examined how reflective cycles can enhance instructional management, student participation, academic achievement, and students’ character formation. A Reflective Action Research (RAR) design was employed through two iterative cycles consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection stages. The study involved one fifth-grade classroom and one teacher, with data collected through observation sheets, student assessments, field notes, and teacher reflective journals. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The findings reveal consistent improvements across all variables from Cycle I to Cycle II. Instructional management became more structured and values-oriented, student participation increased significantly, and learning achievement improved, with mastery learning rising from 65% to 90%. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Descriptive analysis of key determinants of postgraduate education quality in Cambodian universities
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive descriptive analysis of the core determinants influencing postgraduate education quality in Cambodia. Drawing on empirical data from 431 postgraduate students across three leading Cambodian universities, we examine how curriculum structure, faculty competency, research environment, quality assurance, institutional resources, and student satisfaction shape educational experiences. The analysis is anchored in robust theoretical frameworks and employs validated measurement instruments. Results provide foundational insights that inform educational leadership, policymaking, and future research in developing country contexts.

journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: A practical life based digital literacy framework for preservice teachers’ digital transformation
abstract: The rapid digital transformation in preservice teacher education requires future teachers not only to use digital technologies but also to design innovative learning practices that address real-world educational needs. However, many programs still emphasize technical skills rather than the meaningful integration of digital competencies into authentic professional contexts. This study aims to examine how digital literacy is developed among preservice teachers in Islamic higher education institutions and to formulate a practical-life-based digital literacy framework to support their digital transformation. A qualitative multiple case study was conducted at two Indonesian Islamic universities. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with faculty leaders and program administrators, analysis of curriculum documents, student digital portfolios, and observations of technology-enhanced learning environments. Data analysis followed an interactive model and thematic analysis supported by NVivo to ensure systematic coding and interpretation. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: A Systematic analysis of teachers' strategies for promoting resilience and mental health among elementary students following bullying
abstract: The phenomenon of bullying or violence often occurs anywhere, whether at home, in the workplace, or even in educational environments. A safe and peaceful life is a desire longed for by everyone; therefore, with a balanced life, harmonious relationships can be built. However, the reality is often different for those who become victims of bullying, resulting in serious negative impacts on quality of life and mental health. The method used in this study is a systematic literature review (SLR). Regarding this study, teachers must have strategies to overcome the impacts of bullying, which can disturb psychological well-being, such as causing trauma or even depression. Bullying, which in English is called 'bullying,' is often considered trivial and treated as a normal matter. Therefore, this study focuses on three essential aspects, namely, 1) various types of bullying, 2) strategies for teachers to prevent bullying and its consequences, and 3) causes of bullying and ways to maintain students' mental health after bullying. The articles in this research can be used systematically as references to enhance the resilience of students who experience negative impacts from bullying.

journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Innovative learning as a strengthening of 21st-century skills of elementary school students
abstract: 21st-century skills are essential competencies that need to be developed from the elementary school level to prepare students for future challenges. This study aimed to explore the role of innovative learning in strengthening 21st-century skills among elementary school students within the context of the Merdeka Curriculum. This study employed a qualitative case study design. The participants consisted of three elementary school teachers from two districts in Bogor Regency, Indonesia, who had implemented innovative learning practices in their classrooms. Data were collected through open-ended questionnaires and thematically analyzed in NVivo 12 using the stages of open coding, axial coding, and selective coding. The findings revealed that innovative learning practices, such as project-based learning, problem-based learning, collaborative discussion, and the integration of digital media, contributed positively to strengthening students’ critical thinking, creativity, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. Innovative learning also encouraged active student participation, increased students’ confidence, and created more meaningful and student-centered learning experi

journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: The effectiveness of tilawati , ummi , and talaqqi methods on BTQ learning outcomes regarding the gender of elementary students in Bandung
abstract: This study aims to compare students’ learning outcomes in reading and writing the Qur’an (BTQ) based on three teaching methods: Tilawati, Ummi, and Talaqqi. While taking gender differences into account. This study employs a quantitative comparative approach involving 87 elementary school students from three Islamic schools in Bandung. Data were analyzed using SPSS 25, with assumptions tested, and two-way ANOVA, the Median Test, and the Mann-Whitney U Test used as post hoc analyses. The results indicate significant differences in BTQ learning outcomes among the three teaching methods. Post hoc analysis reveals significant differences between the Tilawati and Ummi methods (p = 0.001), the Tilawati and Talaqqi methods (p = 0.010), and the Ummi and Talaqqi methods (p 0.05). Interaction analysis also indicates that gender did not significantly moderate the relationship between learning methods and BTQ learning outcomes (p = 0.367), a finding further supported by profile plots showing relatively parallel patterns across all gender groups. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: An analysis of the curriculum development to improve literacy skills in islamic elementary school based on hilda taba’s framework
abstract: Literacy is an important skill and the foundation for students. Therefore, the school needs to develop a curriculum (planning, implementation, and evaluation) to develop students' literacy skills. This study aims to understand curriculum development to improve literacy skills in Islamic elementary schools. Using a qualitative research approach with a case study design, this study gathers information through interviews with two key informants, analysis of curriculum documents, and observation. The research analysis includes five stages: data collection, coding, data reorganization, data interpretation, and the presentation of findings. Hilda Taba's curriculum development theory serves as a framework for analyzing research data. The results indicate that: (1) the curriculum planning stage is carried out by identifying student needs and exploring community aspirations; (2) the implementation stage of the Madrasah Literacy Movement is realized in the form of a 15-minute daily reading movement, library visits, reading corners, and integration into Indonesian language learning; (3) an evaluation stage once a year to measure the results of curriculum implementation and provide report card

journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Learning in pairs, thinking in shapes: A study on spatial reasoning in elementary school
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of the Power of Two learning model in improving fifth-grade students’ spatial reasoning skills, specifically in understanding plane figures and composite areas. A quantitative approach was employed using an Interrupted Time Series Design, involving 29 students from a public elementary school. The instrument used was the VR-test (Visualization and Relation Test), designed to measure two components of spatial reasoning: spatial visualization and spatial relation. The test was administered in two phases: a pre-test before the intervention and a post-test afterward. The pre-test assessed students’ initial ability to identify and calculate the area of shapes that form composite figures. After the Power of Two intervention, students showed an increase in their average post-test scores, indicating improved spatial reasoning. Statistical analysis using paired and independent-samples t-tests revealed significant differences between pre- and post-test results, confirming the intervention's effectiveness. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Improving elementary teachers' digital pedagogical competence through google classroom training: a one-group pretest-posttest study
abstract: The digital transformation of education represents a significant social shift that requires elementary school teachers to develop strong digital pedagogical competence. As schools increasingly integrate learning management systems into instructional practice, teachers play a central role in shaping how technology influences classroom interaction and learning processes. This study aimed to examine whether Google Classroom training was associated with changes in elementary school teachers' digital pedagogical competence within the broader context of educational digital transformation. A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed involving 30 teachers from a public elementary school in East Java, Indonesia. Data were collected using a validated Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, a paired-samples t-test, and Cohen's d effect size. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Authentic assessment in elementary mathematics: A systematic review of task design, effectiveness, and research gaps
abstract: Authentic assessment has emerged as an approach that bridges assessment practices with meaningful learning in elementary mathematics education. However, studies integrating task design, effectiveness, and research gaps remain limited. This study aims to systematically synthesize authentic assessment in elementary mathematics, focusing on task design, effectiveness, and future research directions. This research employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) guided by PRISMA. Articles were retrieved from Scopus using keywords related to authentic assessment and mathematics education. A total of 48 Scopus-indexed articles were identified, of which 15 were analyzed in depth according to inclusion criteria. Data were analyzed thematically and supported by bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer. The findings indicate that authentic assessment is commonly implemented through performance-based tasks, project-based assessment, portfolios, and rubric-based evaluation. These approaches are effective in enhancing students’ conceptual understanding, critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and engagement in learning. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Effectiveness of digital game-based learning in elementary education: A systematic literature review
abstract: This study aims to systematically synthesize empirical evidence on the effectiveness of Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) in elementary education, focusing on both academic achievement and affective learning outcomes. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA protocol to ensure methodological rigor and transparency. Peer-reviewed empirical articles published between 2021 and 2025 were retrieved from the Scopus database using pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The selection process involved identification, screening, eligibility assessment, and final inclusion stages, resulting in 20 eligible studies. Data were analyzed using thematic synthesis to identify recurring pedagogical patterns and trends in outcomes across studies. The validity of the review process was ensured through clearly defined selection criteria, consistent screening procedures, and cross-checking of extracted data. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Local phenomena-based science learning to enhance science process skills of preservice primary school teachers
abstract: Science process skills (SPS) are essential competencies for preservice primary school teachers because they support scientific inquiry and inquiry-oriented science instruction. However, previous studies indicate limited empirical evidence regarding the use of authentic local environmental phenomena as a field-based inquiry context for developing SPS among prospective teachers. This study aimed to examine how science learning grounded in local phenomena supports SPS development among preservice primary school teachers. A quantitative quasi-experimental design with a pretest–posttest control group structure was employed with 67 participants: an experimental group (n = 34) and a control group (n = 33). The intervention was conducted over six weeks through inquiry activities based on local environmental phenomena in Magetan, East Java, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normalized gain (N-gain), and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA). The results showed that the experimental group achieved higher posttest SPS scores (M = 82.47) than the control group (M = 69.32), with greater improvement reflected in N-gain values (0.60 and 0.30, respectively). journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Innovative science teaching materials based on case-based learning to improve critical thinking skills
abstract: The development of critical thinking skills among pre-service elementary teachers remains a persistent challenge, particularly given the limited availability of instructional materials that explicitly integrate higher-order thinking processes into science instruction. While case-based learning (CBL) has been widely recognized as an effective pedagogical approach, its systematic integration into structured teaching materials in elementary teacher education contexts remains underexplored, especially in local Indonesian settings. This study aims to develop and evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of CBL-oriented science teaching materials designed for pre-service elementary teachers. This research employed a Research and Development (R&D) design based on the Borg and Gall model, involving multiple stages of product validation and field testing. The participants consisted of undergraduate students from a Primary School Teacher Education program. The effectiveness of the developed materials was examined using a quasi-experimental design with pretest–posttest control groups. title: Corrigendum to "Developing picture storybooks assisted by word search puzzle to improve elementary students' indonesian vocabulary mastery"
abstract: This corrigendum addresses two errors in the originally published version of this article. First, the name of the second author in the cited work was inadvertently reversed in the citation metadata. The in-text citation was published as "Kurniawati & Santy, 2022" on pages 448 and 452, whereas it should read "Kurniawati & Yulianti, 2022". Correspondingly, the reference-list entry on page 463 was published as "Kurniawati, W., & Santy, Y. (2022)" and should read "Kurniawati, W., & Yulianti, S. (2022)", reflecting the correct author name, Santy Yulianti. Second, in Table 3, "Results of media expert assessment of picture storybooks," on page 454, the percentage for the "Language and readability" aspect was incorrectly printed as "8.,5%"; the correct value is "87,5%". These corrections do not affect the results, interpretation, or conclusions of the article. The authors sincerely apologize for these errors and any inconvenience they may have caused. The online version of the article has been amended accordingly.

journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Analysis bibliometrics study reasoning mathematical in mathematics education: trends, structures, and implications for elementary school education
abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental competency in mathematics education that supports students' logical, critical, and systematic thinking skills. Along with technological advancements and the growing demands of twenty-first-century learning, research on mathematical reasoning has expanded significantly and become increasingly multidisciplinary. This study employed a bibliometric analysis to map the global development of research on mathematical reasoning in mathematics education. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database using the keywords "mathematical reasoning" and "learning". A total of 685 documents published between 1979 and 2026 were analyzed using Biblioshiny. The analysis focused on identifying publication trends, thematic structures, collaboration patterns, and the geographical distribution of research contributions. The results reveal a substantial increase in publications, particularly since 2006, with research productivity peaking in 2023. The field is organized around three major domains: pedagogical aspects of mathematics learning, mathematical modeling development, and technology integration, including artificial intelligence and machine learning. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Utilizing digital citizenship education to strengthen elementary students' civic skills: a systematic literature review
abstract: Digital Citizenship Education (DCE) has emerged as a critical component in developing civic skills among elementary students amid rapid digital transformation. This study aims to examine how DCE is implemented across diverse educational contexts, identify technological, pedagogical, and socio-cultural challenges in its implementation, and explore effective practices that enhance students' digital literacy and civic engagement. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with bibliometric analysis guided by the PRISMA framework, this study analyses 66 articles from the Scopus database and further examines them using VOSviewer to map citation networks, international collaboration, and keyword relationships. The findings reveal a significant upward trend in DCE publications since 2021, with the majority of publications originating from Asian and Western countries. DCE is operationalized through digital-based learning, inclusive multimedia approaches, and the integration of cyber wisdom. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: The effectiveness of storytelling in improving language literacy in children aged 5–6 years to support primary school readiness
abstract: This study examines the effect of storytelling on the language and literacy skills of children aged 5–6 years, as a foundation for school readiness. Language literacy is an essential component of school readiness because it supports children's ability to understand instructions, communicate effectively, participate in classroom interactions, and engage in early learning activities when entering primary school. However, numerous preschool children still experience difficulties with listening, speaking, vocabulary, retelling, early reading, and early writing. Therefore, effective learning strategies are needed to strengthen children's language literacy before transitioning to formal education. This study employs a quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group design. The participants consisted of 20 children aged 5–6 years from TK Negeri Pembina V Pekanbaru, divided into an experimental group (n = 10) and a control group (n = 10). Data were collected using an observation sheet comprising 18 items covering six language literacy indicators: listening, speaking, vocabulary, retelling, early reading, and early writing. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Developing a multicultural education-based assessment instrument for Indonesian language learning in fourth-grade elementary schools
abstract: This study developed a multicultural education-based assessment instrument for fourth-grade Indonesian language learning that integrates reading-comprehension assessment with indicators of tolerance, empathy, cooperation, and cultural appreciation. A research and development design adapted from Gall et al. was implemented in eight stages: needs analysis, information gathering, product design, expert validation, revision, limited trial, product refinement, and field implementation. The study involved three experts, five Grade IV teachers, and 108 students across the development stages; the final implementation and student response testing involved 77 students from three elementary schools in Semarang. The final product consists of an assessment blueprint, reading-comprehension tasks, and a multicultural attitude rubric. Expert validation yielded an overall mean of 92%, indicating high validity. Teacher practicality testing reached 96%, indicating that the instrument was feasible and easy to use. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Teachers' beliefs about teaching and learning and their implications for meaningful learning practices in elementary school in Bandung: a phenomenological study
abstract: This study aims to explore teachers' beliefs and their implications for meaningful learning practices in elementary schools using a qualitative phenomenological approach. The participants consisted of ten elementary school teachers in Bandung, Indonesia, from both public and private schools, who were purposively selected based on the criteria that (a) they are recognized as highly dedicated teachers and (b) they have more than ten years of teaching experience. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and document analysis, and subsequently analyzed and categorized into thematic findings. The results reveal several patterns related to teachers' beliefs, including (1) teacher–student relationships as the foundation of learning, (2) knowledge construction through connecting new learning with students' prior experiences to promote meaningful learning, (3) teachers' flexibility in adapting instructional strategies to students' needs, (4) teachers' positive beliefs about the potential of every student, and (5) teachers' beliefs as a driver of instructional innovation. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Montessori method assisted by activity books for enchancing social skills and information literacy
abstract: Amid the demands of the 21st century, elementary school students often face challenges in interpersonal cooperation and in processing critical information. This study empirically examines the effect of the Montessori Method, supported by a Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) activity book, on the social skills and information literacy of sixth-grade students. Using a quantitative, quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent control group, the study involved a sample of 56 students at SDN Jatisari, utilizing validated questionnaires and objective tests, and was analyzed using MANOVA. Descriptive results showed that the experimental group achieved significantly higher mean scores for social skills (M = 82.07; N-Gain = 0.61) and information literacy (M = 91.89) than the control group (M = 59.25; N-Gain = 0.04; M = 68.50). The MANOVA simultaneous test confirmed high statistical significance (p = 0.000; Wilks' Lambda = 0.066) with robust univariate R-squared values of 0.932 and 0.676. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Self-compassion and maternal involvement: an analysis of the relationship in parents of elementary students with special needs
abstract: Parents of children with special needs often experience emotional and psychological challenges in parenting, making self-compassion an essential internal resource that may influence parental involvement. This study aims to examine the relationship between self-compassion and maternal involvement among parents of children with special needs enrolled in elementary school. A quantitative correlational design was used involving 165 parents in Langkat, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), the Nurturant Mothering Scale (NMS), and the Mother Involvement Scale (MIS), and analyzed using the Pearson Product–Moment correlation test. The findings reveal a significant positive relationship between self-compassion and affective maternal involvement (r = 0.159, p 0.05). Although significant, both correlations were weak. These findings indicate that self-compassion may support emotional warmth and behavioral involvement in parenting children with special needs. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Effectiveness of STS-C-based multimodal science materials on primary students' digital science literacy and global character
abstract: This study analyzes the effectiveness of Science, Technology, Society, and Culture (STS-C) based multimodal science materials in enhancing digital science literacy and global character among fifth-grade students. This quasi-experimental study employed a Non-equivalent Control Group design involving 64 students. Data gathered via digital science literacy tests, global character questionnaires, and observation sheets were analyzed using ANCOVA and N-Gain scores. The experimental group showed a significant increase in digital science literacy (mean post-test: 88.65; N-Gain: 0.74, high) and global character (mean post-test: 84.30; N-Gain: 0.58, medium). journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: The use of cloud-based learning media and its implications for elementary students' digital literacy
abstract: The use of cloud-based learning media is a relevant digital learning strategy for supporting the development of digital literacy among elementary students. This study aims to analyze the digital literacy skills of elementary school students using cloud-based learning media in Kulon Progo. The study employs a qualitative approach, involving elementary school students, classroom teachers, and ICT administrators as participants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, learning observations, and documentation studies, subsequently analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing using source and technique triangulation. The results reveal that students are accustomed to using digital devices to support learning, especially in accessing information, taking online quizzes, and completing cloud-based assignments. The use of cloud-based media contributes to increased student engagement, motivation, and learning experiences. However, the ability to critically evaluate digital information, creativity in producing digital content, and the use of artificial intelligence-based technology still require strengthening. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: The effectiveness of the SEPTIA model integrating Taneyan Lanjhang local values on elementary students’ social-cultural literacy
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the SEPTIA model (Solving Education through Problem, Tradition, and Indigenous Approach) in enhancing fourth-grade students’ socio-cultural literacy in elementary natural and social science studies (IPAS). The model integrates Problem-Based Learning (PBL) with the local cultural values of Taneyan Lanjhang to develop four dimensions of socio-cultural literacy: intellectual (analysis of social issues), social (empathy and tolerance), cultural (appreciation of local values), and collaborative (cooperative problem-solving skills). A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control-group design was implemented, involving 50 fourth-grade students from two elementary schools in Pamekasan (25 in the experimental group and 25 in the control group). Data were collected using a validated socio-cultural literacy test and structured observation sheets, and were analyzed through paired-sample t-tests, independent-sample t-tests, and Cohen’s d effect size. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Ecosystem-based IPAS modules: traces of innovation by pre-service elementary school teachers in 21st-century learning
abstract: This study examines how pre-service elementary teachers develop pedagogical competence through a project-based learning experience involving the design of ecosystem-based IPAS (integrated science and social studies) modules. The study aims to explore (1) the instructional design process, (2) the characteristics and quality of the modules produced, and (3) participants' perceptions of their pedagogical competence development. A qualitative case study design was employed involving 30 pre-service teachers enrolled in a primary teacher education program. Data were collected through classroom observations, document analysis of instructional modules, and semi-structured interviews, and were analyzed thematically. Module quality was further examined using expert validation criteria. The findings indicate that pre-service teachers demonstrated emerging pedagogical competence, particularly in aligning content with learning objectives and adapting instructional materials to students' characteristics. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Articulate storyline-based multimedia development to improve the mathematical representation skills of grade V elementary school students
abstract: This research is motivated by the limited use of interactive multimedia, specifically designed to improve elementary school students' mathematical representation skills in integer operations materials. Previous studies have generally focused on improving learning outcomes without emphasizing mathematical representation as a key competency. Therefore, this study aims to develop and test the effectiveness of Articulate Storyline-based multimedia specifically designed to support students' mathematical representation abilities. This research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The study subjects were elementary school grade V students (n = 34) with an evaluation design using a one-group pretest–posttest. The primary instrument was a mathematical representation test, constructed based on NCTM indicators and operationalized as items assessing students' abilities to translate, interpret, and construct representations. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: Strengthening ecoliteracy through eco comic in peat conservation efforts in Kampung Jati Baru Siak
abstract: Environmental education plays an important role in developing ecological literacy among primary school students, particularly in regions characterized by unique local ecosystems. However, environmental learning materials often remain disconnected from students’ everyday environmental experiences. This study aimed to evaluate the implementation of the Eco Comic program as a contextual learning medium for strengthening ecological literacy related to peatland conservation among primary school students in Kampung Jati Baru, Siak Regency, Riau Province, Indonesia. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with a program evaluation design. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and learning evaluations involving students, teachers, environmental practitioners, illustrators, and village officials. An initial needs assessment involving 30 students was conducted to identify students’ prior understanding of peatland ecosystems, while the implementation stage involved 65 students from three elementary schools. journal_name: Primary: Jurnal Pendidikan Guru Sekolah Dasar
title: An analysis of the educational material needs for children with special needs: perspectives from students and tutors of the preservice teacher program at Universitas Terbuka
abstract: This study investigates the expectations of students and tutors in the Primary School Teacher Education (PGSD) program at Universitas Terbuka regarding instructional resources for the Special Needs Children Education (ABK) course. A needs analysis was conducted through surveys and interviews to inform the development of adaptive and inclusive materials aligned with the PGSD curriculum. Results show that 88.77% of students and 84.5% of tutors emphasized the importance of inclusive education in ABK materials. Moreover, 78.56% of students and 81% of tutors agreed on updating previous resources. In terms of accessibility, 90% of students and 66.6% of tutors considered earlier materials conceptually rich. The visual presentation remained appealing to 55% of students and 61.9% of tutors, and grammar was deemed clear by 66.3% of students and 57.1% of tutors. Divergent views emerged on interactivity: 40.8% of students found older resources less engaging, while 61.9% of tutors disagreed. title: Ruma Bolon -based IPAS instruction for strengthening elementary students' critical thinking skills
abstract: This study examines how Ruma Bolon-based IPAS instruction can strengthen elementary students' critical thinking skills while sustaining Toba Batak cultural values as learning resources. Using an explanatory mixed-methods design, the study involved 30 fourth-grade students in Medan Helvetia District. Quantitative data were gathered through a validated critical-thinking test, supported by interviews, classroom observations, questionnaires, and documentation. Instrument validation showed strong content validity (CVI = 0.91), valid item coefficients (0.42-0.81), and high reliability for the critical-thinking test (Cronbach's alpha = 0.88) and student perception questionnaire (Cronbach's alpha = 0.86). The quantitative findings showed increases in analytical skills from 40% to 70%, synthesis skills from 50% to 75%, and evaluation skills from 60% to 80%; the average score rose from approximately 65% to 85%. title: Learning trauma in elementary social studies classrooms ( IPS ): a phenomenological inquiry
abstract: Emotional experiences significantly shape students’ engagement and academic identity, yet subject-specific learning trauma in elementary Social Studies remains underexplored. This study explored the lived experiences of elementary students who encountered learning trauma—defined as a pedagogical phenomenon of repeated emotional distress, not a clinical diagnosis—during Social Studies instruction. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with eight purposively selected students (grades 4–6) from two elementary schools in Pekanbaru, Indonesia, who reported experiencing repeated negative emotions during Social Studies lessons. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s phenomenological method. Four essential themes emerged: fear of public humiliation, anxiety toward evaluation and memorization, emotional withdrawal, and defensive avoidance behaviors. These experiences were shaped by evaluative classroom practices and teacher-centered instruction, not extreme events. title: Beyond the surface: a narrative inquiry into the transformation of prospective teachers' pedagogical content knowledge for early numeracy
abstract: This study explores how prospective teachers' Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK) for early numeracy is articulated and reconstructed across different stages of teacher education. While prior research has examined PCK development, limited attention has been given to how prospective teachers at varying stages conceptualize and integrate numeracy knowledge within practice. Addressing this gap, the study aims to compare narrative representations of PCK among prospective teachers at early, intermediate, and final stages of their preparation. Adopting a qualitative narrative inquiry approach, data were collected from six participants through in-depth interviews and classroom observations within a single semester. Rather than tracking the same individuals over time, the study contrasts developmental perspectives across stages. title: A hybrid systematic review and bibliometric analysis of character education in science and social studies
abstract: Character education is increasingly crucial amid growing social complexity. However, its integration within science and social studies remains fragmented. This study aims to map research trends, identify dominant character values, and examine key gaps in this field. A hybrid approach combining a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis was applied to 131 Scopus-indexed articles (2016–2025). The findings reveal a growing body of research with a fragmented yet interconnected intellectual structure. Five categories of character values were identified, with social–civic and moral–ethical values as the most dominant, followed by scientific, environmental, and social–emotional values. Six main pedagogical approaches were integrated learning, project-based learning, and citizenship-based approaches. Key gaps include the absence of an integrated conceptual framework, limited use of experimental and longitudinal designs, and insufficient development of context-sensitive character assessment tools. title: Development of an innovative differentiated learning model for inclusive education in the independent elementary school curriculum
abstract: This study addresses the limited availability of empirically validated differentiated learning models for inclusive elementary classrooms within the Merdeka Curriculum. It aims to develop and examine the feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness of an innovative differentiated learning model for Indonesian language instruction in an inclusive elementary school. The study employed research and development using the ADDIE model and involved two Indonesian language teachers, 67 fifth-grade students, and three expert validators at SD Santo Petrus Medan Johor. The resulting products consist of a teacher handbook and a student workbook integrating diagnostic assessment, learner-profile mapping, differentiated content-process-product pathways, and adaptive assessment. Expert validation placed the model in the highly feasible category (86.75%). Practicality was also high, as indicated by teacher responses (88.40%) and student responses (85.60%). Effectiveness testing revealed an increase in learning outcomes from 70.85 to 82.30 with a moderate N-gain of 0.39, while students’ social skills improved by 15.20%. title: Backround of the Study Teachers’ Strategies for Implementing the Merdeka Curriculum in Elementery Schools in 3T Areas : A literature Review
abstract: This study is motivated by educational disparities in 3T areas (disadvantaged, frontier, and outermost regions), which are characterized by limited infrastructure, restricted access to technology, and insufficient teacher competence in implementing the Merdeka Curriculum. These conditions necessitate the development of adaptive, context-specific learning strategies. This study aims to analyze adaptive teaching strategies and examine the relationships among contextual challenges, pedagogical adaptation, instructional strategies, and their implications for teaching practices. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach based on 15 relevant scholarly articles. The findings indicate that the dominant strategy is contextual learning (26.7%), followed by Project-Based Learning (20%) and differentiated instruction (13.3%). These results suggest that teachers develop flexible strategies by utilizing local contexts and adapting instructional methods accordingly. title: Optimizing IPAS learning to improve learning outcomes through the application of the teaching at the right level approach integrated with quizizz
abstract: This classroom action research examined whether the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach could improve fourth-grade students' learning outcomes in IPAS, especially on the topic of ethnic and cultural diversity, at UPT SDN 066047 Medan Helvetia. The study involved 14 students and was conducted in two cycles. The mean score increased from 57 in the pre-cycle to 76 in Cycle I and 89 in Cycle II, while classical mastery improved from 43% to 79% and finally to 100%. The study addresses a gap in the Indonesian elementary education literature, where TaRL has been discussed more often in literacy and numeracy than in interdisciplinary IPAS learning for lower- and middle-grade students. Its contribution lies in showing how diagnostic grouping, focused reinforcement, and cycle-based reflection can be operationalized in a real classroom to improve conceptual understanding of a contextually meaningful IPAS topic. The findings suggest that TaRL is not only effective at improving test performance but also a useful adaptive pedagogical strategy for elementary classrooms with heterogeneous readiness levels.
